personal_landing.title: I turn an ambiguous signal into a decision that can be examined.
personal_landing.lede: This synthetic case demonstrates how I structure a question, test the evidence, separate description from causality, and make the next action explicit.
personal_landing.evidence_body: Across eight frozen weeks, positive feedback reaches 83.4%; billing clarity and response time account for 57.1% of negative items.
personal_landing.method_body: Define the period, preserve units, label uncertainty, and use color only when it carries a stable meaning.

case_study_report.title: Which friction deserves the next improvement cycle?
case_study_report.abstract: A synthetic eight-week benchmark tests how descriptive feedback can support a bounded decision without pretending to prove causality.
case_study_report.question_body: Should the next cycle prioritize billing clarity and response time while preserving the current positive trajectory?
case_study_report.data_body: 1,165 synthetic feedback items across 2026-W15 to 2026-W22, classified as positive, neutral, or negative.
case_study_report.method_body: Compare weekly sentiment counts, then inspect the distribution of negative-feedback drivers. Use direct labels and redundant marks so interpretation does not depend on color alone.
case_study_report.finding_body: Positive feedback represents 83.4% of the sample. Billing clarity and response time account for 57.1% of negative items.
case_study_report.limit_body: The fixture is descriptive and synthetic. It supports prioritization, not a causal claim or a real client result.
case_study_report.decision_body: Prioritize billing clarity and response time as the next bounded improvement cycle, then review six additional weeks of feedback.
